chunks.text: This project aims to collect Near Eastern royal epics, i.e. narratives about kings. So far, it includes only one entry, the Epic of Zimri-Lim. The project is currently only a work in progress                You can view the project's content  here  [/nere/pager] .
Near Eastern Royal Epics  » Epic of Zimrī-Lîm

The Epic of  Zimrī-Lîm is an Akkadian text inscribed on a single clay tablet, discovered in the ruins of the city of Mari in Syria (modern Tell Hariri), praising one of the kings of this city, Zimrī-Lîm (ruled ca. 1780–1758 BC). Only one exemplar of this text has been discovered to date (A. 3152+M.5665+unnumbered fragment), and it does not belong to the most famous works of ancient literature. The tablet was located in the Deir ez-Zor museum form where it has been evacuated in 2015. The current location is unknown.                  This project was created hand in hand with my master's thesis on the Epic of Zimrī-Lîm. This thesis currently works as a commentary of this epic. In the near future, I hope to transfer some parts of the thesis into the contents of this project. The thesis in pdf is availiable  here  [https://www.academia.edu/70208904/The_Epic_of_Zimr%C4%AB_L%C3%AEm] .                You can view the Epic of Zimri-Lim  here  [/nere/Q009326] .
